peer_results.rationale: The provided AMD candidates discuss amortization of intangibles (amd_2024_7_D034) and Client segment operating income (amd_2024_7_D025). Intel's disclosure focuses on the broad 'Intel Products' segment operating expense decline due to cost reductions. AMD's amortization topic is distinct from operating expense drivers. AMD's Client segment income improvement is driven by revenue increases partially offset by higher expenses, which does not provide a comparable narrative of expense *decline* or specific cost-reduction measure impacts on the total segment expense level in the same manner as Intel's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom (AVGO) identify restructuring and cost reduction activities as key components of their operating expense changes. Intel's operating expense decline is 'primarily driven by various cost-reduction measures' (intc_2024_7_P043_S001). Broadcom explicitly breaks out restructuring charges within operating expenses, which increased to $1,533 million in 2024, 'primarily [consisting] of employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger' (avgo_2024_7_P052_S001, avgo_2024_7_P052_S002). While Intel's cost reductions led to a net decrease in expenses, Broadcom's cost reduction activities (alongside other charges) resulted in a significant increase in recognized restructuring costs, illustrating that 'cost-reduction measures' can manifest as either operational efficiency gains or immediate restructuring charges.

sentences.text: Total Intel Products operating expenses were $12.2 billion in 2023, down $3.1 billion from 2022, primarily driven by various cost-reduction measures across all of our Intel Products operating segments.
Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million and $244 million in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The fiscal year 2024 charges primarily included employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger.

peer_results.rationale: The provided MU candidates discuss EBU operating income changes driven by pricing, volume, and cost reductions (mu_2024_7_D014, mu_2024_7_D018). While MU mentions 'cost reductions' as an offset to ASP declines, this is part of a broader operating income explanation involving revenue dynamics. Intel's disclosure is specifically about the magnitude and drivers of the operating expense *decline* itself ($3.1 billion drop). MU's disclosure does not isolate operating expense changes as the primary driver of a net financial result in the same way, nor does it provide a comparable breakdown of expense line items like Intel's CCG/DCAI/NEX specific decreases.

comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses increased in fiscal year 2024 due to employee growth and compensation increases; fiscal year 2023 included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose changes in their operating expenses and attribute significant drivers to cost-related actions or employment changes, though in opposite directions. Intel reports a $3.1 billion decline in Intel Products operating expenses driven by 'cost-reduction measures across all of our Intel Products operating segments' (intc_2024_7_P043_S001). In contrast, NVIDIA reports an increase in operating expenses driven by 'growth in employees and compensation increases' (nvda_2024_7_P024_S001), while noting a specific $1.4 billion non-recurring acquisition termination charge in the prior year (nvda_2024_7_P024_S002). The comparison highlights divergent operational cost trajectories: Intel's focused reduction versus NVIDIA's growth-driven expansion and one-time restructuring-like charges.

sentences.text: Total Intel Products operating expenses were $12.2 billion in 2023, down $3.1 billion from 2022, primarily driven by various cost-reduction measures across all of our Intel Products operating segments.
Operating expenses increased for fiscal year 2024, driven by growth in employees and compensation increases.
Fiscal year 2023 also included a $1.4 billion acquisition termination charge related to the proposed Arm transaction.

peer_results.rationale: The provided QCOM candidates discuss fiscal 2023 other expenses (qcom_2024_7_D015) and fiscal 2024 SG&A expense drivers (qcom_2024_7_D013). Intel's disclosure is for fiscal year 2023 operating expenses. QCOM's SG&A drivers (sales/marketing, deferred comp, share-based comp) are different in nature from Intel's broad 'cost-reduction measures' across product segments. QCOM's 2023 other expenses (restructuring/impairment) are also not directly comparable to Intel's operating expense decline driven by ongoing operational cost reductions.
